https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Warnings over flammable emollient cream after death of Mexborough man in fire
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
A grandfather died after his clothes caught fire due to the flammable skin cream he used, an investigation has found.
Jim Rownsley, 89, was found dead after a fire started by a gas heater at his home on Kempton Gardens, in Mexborough, Doncaster, on 20 February.
It is believed residue from the emollient cream he used made his clothes more flammable.
Mr Rownsley's granddaughter Sherrie-Leigh Higgins said: “You never think something like this is going to happen to your family until it does.
“My grandad always used his gas heater to stay warm but we didn’t know that the cream he used for his legs could be so dangerous."
Emollient creams, which are also available as lotions, gels, and sprays can be water-based, paraffin-based, or contain natural oils and are used to treat conditions including eczema.
They soak into clothes if used regularly and can become a fire risk.
Ms Higgins added: “If someone you love uses these creams, please make sure you and they know how they can keep themselves safe. I don’t want anyone else to go through the same trauma that we did.”
Chris Tyler, manager of South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue’s community safety team, said the creams were not flammable on their own, but a "build-up"  on bedding, clothing, and dressings could make them a fire risk.
He added: “What this means is that, in cases where somebody uses these creams on a regular basis or spends an extended amount of time in their bed or armchair, their fire risk can increase dramatically.
“Anyone using emollient or skin creams regularly should keep well away from fire, naked flames, or heat sources."
The fire was out on arrival and an investigation was carried out, which was completed by 6pm.

https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Parents' sepsis warning after death of three-year-old Chesterfield boy
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
The parents of a three-year-old boy who died from sepsis after being misdiagnosed say they struggle to deal with the "madness" caused by his death.
Oscar Neillings died at Chesterfield Royal Hospital in November 2023, about a week after contracting a streptococcus A infection.
An inquest at Chesterfield Coroner's Court has heard two GPs had mistakenly diagnosed his cold symptoms as a viral infection before he was referred to hospital.
Hospital staff then failed to administer antibiotics for more than two hours after he was admitted.
A jury found on Friday that neglect had contributed to his death.
Oscar's mother Stephanie said she and her husband, Mark, try to maintain normality for their other two children, Poppy and Maxwell.
She said: "It's so hard to cover everything up. I think we both have got this amazing mask that we put on to cover everything with a smile.
"I can't believe this is our life. It's utter madness."
The inquest heard Oscar, who was described by his parents as "a ball of energy" who was "fun loving", developed a cold about a week before his death from which he never recovered.
As his symptoms worsened, they twice called the NHS 111 helpline, leading to separate out-of-hours GP appointments.
Both doctors said Oscar had a viral infection and did not think he needed to be referred to hospital, the court was told.
It was only when he developed abdominal pain, vomiting, and breathing difficulties that a third GP referred him to hospital on 8 November 2023.
Medical experts told the hearing Oscar’s care was fragmented and lacked urgency. He died from a cardiac arrest the same day.
What are the symptoms of sepsis?
Sepsis is a serious condition that arises when the body's response to an infection injures its own tissues and organs.
It happens when the immune system reacts to an infection in an extreme way.
The main symptoms are:
Fever or low body temperature
Chills and shivering:
Rapid breathing or shortness of breath
Fast heart rate
Changes in mental status
Skin changes
Rash
"No one can understand, unless they've been through similar, what is actually going on inside," Mrs Neillings said.
"He was just so wonderful and it's so hard to believe that he's gone. I don't think I actually do believe that.
"We were meant to be planning for his school place in the December but instead we were planning his funeral."
The couple are warning other parents to be aware of the signs of sepsis and are calling for the condition to be given greater recognition.
Mrs Neillings said: "It should be treated as a medical emergency, the same as a heart attack of stroke, and that is what the UK Sepsis Trust are pushing for.
"If the general public are aware and they can actually go into a medical environment and say 'could this be sepsis?' and actually use the word, because as soon as it's out there then it gets people thinking."
Mark Neillings, Oscar's father, said: "We want recognition of sepsis and how drastically things can change. We want awareness in hospitals, especially at smaller hospitals."

https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-05.title: Reform UK councillor Ian Cooper confirmed as leader of Staffordshire County Council
https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-05.text:
Reform UK has formally taken control of Staffordshire County Council following its success in the local elections, appointing Cllr Ian Cooper (Perrycrofts Tamworth) as Leader and Cllr Martin Murray (Cannock Town Cannock Chase) as Deputy Leader.
The party now faces the challenge of turning campaign rhetoric into day-to-day results - managing local services, infrastructure, and budgets across one of England’s largest counties.
It marks the first time Reform UK has been in control of a major local authority.
Cllr Cooper, who has lived in Tamworth since 1996 and brings over 35 years of business experience, was the first Reform UK candidate for Tamworth in the 2024 General Election.
He will be tasked with leading the council through mounting financial pressure and long-standing service issues.
The 2025 election result for Staffordshire County Council was:
Reform UK: 49
Conservative: 10
Green: 1
Labour, Labour & Co-operative Party: 1
Stafford Borough Independents: 1
From road repairs and adult social care to school places and housing demand, Staffordshire residents will expect delivery, not just disruption.
While Reform UK has gained ground nationally by promising bold reforms, many of its flagship policies fall outside the remit of county councils.
That means Cllr Cooper and his team will need to work within existing structures, navigating the realities of local governance while trying to offer a visibly different approach.
Deputy Leader Cllr Martin Murray, representing Cannock Town, will play a key role in shaping how the party governs at a local level, balancing budget demands with public expectations.
With four years ahead, Staffordshire becomes a high-stakes testing ground for Reform UK.
Voters will be watching closely to see whether the party can make the transition from protest vote to practical government.
